doc.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002

title: Is there a Detroit sound; Flanagan, Burrell and Detroit friends
summary: Jordan says Detroit musicians are originals, naming Tommy Flanagan, Kenny Burrell, Hank Jones and Milt Jackson.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay. Was there a Detroit sound? Do you think there is a Detroit sound?

Woooah, yeah. We’re all originals. I mean most of them. Look at Tommy Flanagan. I grew up with Tommy and Barry and Kenny Burrell and we are all very close. And our hero at the time, from Detroit, was Hank Jones and Milt Jackson. Because Milt Jackson had gone off with Dizzy Gillespie and Hank Jones had been out there for a while, even though he wasn’t originally from Detroit. So we had our own — we were struggling with this music, you know, going around. I should say I was struggling with it. Because the prejudice in Detroit was not to be believed.
